paragraphs.source_en: A cat’s four legs are as good as nonexistent. Wherever it walks, it has never once made an awkward sound. It is as though treading the air, traveling upon clouds, striking a chime beneath the water, playing a zither in a cave, or tasting the wondrous flavor of ghee and knowing warmth and cold for itself beyond all words. I pay no heed at all to ordinary Western houses, model kitchens, the rickshawman’s wife, manservants, cooking maids, young ladies, housemaids, Madam Nose, or Madam’s husband. I go wherever I wish, hear whatever I wish to hear, then stick out my tongue, flick my tail, bristle my whiskers, and return at leisure. In this art especially, I may be called the foremost master in Japan. I even suspect myself of possessing the bloodline of those goblin cats that so often appear in old illustrated storybooks. They say a toad’s forehead conceals a luminous pearl, but in my tail is packed an ancestral miraculous medicine that lets me scorn not only deities, Buddhism, lust, impermanence, and such notions, but even all the people under heaven. Unseen and unsuspected, I roamed at will through the corridors of the Kaneda house. That was far easier than a guardian deity trampling a block of konnyaku jelly flat. Thinking this, I could not help admiring my own powers. I thought this must be entirely thanks to the care I always lavished on my tail, and that I must never again treat it lightly. I therefore resolved to worship my Tail Bodhisattva and pray for the long continuance of feline fortune. I lowered my head and looked, but something seemed a little off. I had to behold my own tail and bow to it three times. I turned around to look at my tail, but naturally the tail turned along with my body. I twisted my head to catch up with it, but it kept the same distance and ran on ahead. Plainly this tail is a spirit capable of enclosing heaven and earth within its three inches; it is utterly beyond my power to deal with. I kept chasing my own tail for seven and a half turns, then grew so tired that I gave up. I felt somewhat dizzy, and had quite lost track of where I was. No matter; I went wandering wildly about the corridor. Suddenly I heard Nose’s voice from behind a sliding screen. Thinking this must be the very place I was looking for, I stopped, cocked both ears sideways, and listened with bated breath. “For a poor teacher, isn’t he insolent!” Nose said this in her characteristic shrill voice. “Yes, an insolent fellow. We’ll tease him a little to teach him a lesson. There are students from my home province at that school where he teaches.” This was Mr. Kaneda’s voice. “Who are they?” Nose asked. “Tsuneki Pinsuke and Fukuchi Kishago are at that school, so I’ll have them tease him.” I do not know where Mr. Kaneda’s native place is, but I was somewhat surprised that it seemed stocked entirely with people bearing such odd names. Mr. Kaneda went on and asked, “Is that fellow an English teacher?” “According to the rickshawman’s wife, he teaches something called English readers as his specialty.” “Damn him, he’s bound to be a worthless teacher anyway.”

units.source_en: A cat’s four legs are as good as nonexistent.
units.source_zh: 猫的四条腿虽有如无。

units.source_en: Wherever it walks, it has never once made an awkward sound.
units.source_zh: 不管走到哪里，从来没有发出过笨拙的声响。

units.source_en: It is as though treading the air, traveling upon clouds, striking a chime beneath the water, playing a zither in a cave, or tasting the wondrous flavor of ghee and knowing warmth and cold for itself beyond all words.
units.source_zh: 它宛如凌空飞腾，踏云而行，宛如水中击磬、洞中鼓瑟，宛如饱尝醍醐妙味而冷暖自知一样。

units.source_en: I pay no heed at all to ordinary Western houses, model kitchens, the rickshawman’s wife, manservants, cooking maids, young ladies, housemaids, Madam Nose, or Madam’s husband.
units.source_zh: 我根本不把什么平庸的洋房、模范的厨房、车夫的老婆、听差、烧饭的女仆、小姐、侍女、鼻子夫人、夫人的丈夫放在眼里。

units.source_en: I go wherever I wish, hear whatever I wish to hear, then stick out my tongue, flick my tail, bristle my whiskers, and return at leisure.
units.source_zh: 我想去哪儿就去哪儿，把想听的都听到之后，伸伸舌头，甩甩尾巴，竖竖胡须，然后悠悠然回来就是了。

units.source_en: In this art especially, I may be called the foremost master in Japan.
units.source_zh: 我尤其对于此道，可谓日本第一名手。

units.source_en: I even suspect myself of possessing the bloodline of those goblin cats that so often appear in old illustrated storybooks.
units.source_zh: 甚至连我自己也在怀疑我是否具有经常出现在草双纸故事中那猫精的血统哩。

units.source_en: They say a toad’s forehead conceals a luminous pearl, but in my tail is packed an ancestral miraculous medicine that lets me scorn not only deities, Buddhism, lust, impermanence, and such notions, but even all the people under heaven.
units.source_zh: 听说蛤蟆的额头上藏有一颗夜明珠，可我的尾巴上却藏有祖传的妙药，这种药不但可以使我蔑视那些神祇、释教、色欲、无常等等观念，甚至也可以把满天下的人都不当回事。

units.source_en: Unseen and unsuspected, I roamed at will through the corridors of the Kaneda house.
units.source_zh: 我人不知鬼不觉地在金田家廊子里闯来闯去。

units.source_en: That was far easier than a guardian deity trampling a block of konnyaku jelly flat.
units.source_zh: 这比金刚力士踩烂一块魔芋豆腐还要容易得多。

units.source_en: Thinking this, I could not help admiring my own powers.
units.source_zh: 想到这里，我不能不佩服起自己的力量来。

units.source_en: I thought this must be entirely thanks to the care I always lavished on my tail, and that I must never again treat it lightly.
units.source_zh: 我想，这完全是托我平时十分珍惜自己尾巴的福，我再也不该将它等闲视之了。

units.source_en: I therefore resolved to worship my Tail Bodhisattva and pray for the long continuance of feline fortune.
units.source_zh: 于是我决心向我的尾巴大菩萨礼拜一番，来祈祷“猫运长久”。

units.source_en: I lowered my head and looked, but something seemed a little off.
units.source_zh: 我低下头看了看，好像有点不对头。

units.source_en: I had to behold my own tail and bow to it three times.
units.source_zh: 我必须瞻仰一下自己的尾巴，向它三叩首。

units.source_en: I turned around to look at my tail, but naturally the tail turned along with my body.
units.source_zh: 我转过身想看看尾巴，可尾巴也自然随着身子转。

units.source_en: I twisted my head to catch up with it, but it kept the same distance and ran on ahead.
units.source_zh: 我扭过头去，想追上它，可它还是保持相同的间隔，跑在前头。

units.source_en: Plainly this tail is a spirit capable of enclosing heaven and earth within its three inches; it is utterly beyond my power to deal with.
units.source_zh: 看来这尾巴的确是将天地玄黄都收到它那三寸之中的灵物，我是绝对对付不了的。

units.source_en: I kept chasing my own tail for seven and a half turns, then grew so tired that I gave up.
units.source_zh: 我一直在追自己的尾巴，追了七回半，实在太累，只好作罢。

units.source_en: I felt somewhat dizzy, and had quite lost track of where I was.

ja.t: がくらむ。どこにいるのだかちょっと

units.source_zh: 我多少有点天旋地转，简直不知道现在是在哪儿啦。

units.source_en: No matter; I went wandering wildly about the corridor.
units.source_zh: 管它呢，我在廊子里到处乱闯。

units.source_en: Suddenly I heard Nose’s voice from behind a sliding screen.
units.source_zh: 忽然听到拉门里传来鼻子的声音。

units.source_en: Thinking this must be the very place I was looking for, I stopped, cocked both ears sideways, and listened with bated breath.
units.source_zh: 我想这正是我要找的地方嘛，于是我停下来，把左右两只耳朵斜着掀动了一下，屏息静气地听着。

units.source_en: “For a poor teacher, isn’t he insolent!”
units.source_zh: “一个穷教员，竟然这样狂傲！”

units.source_en: Nose said this in her characteristic shrill voice.
units.source_zh: 鼻子发出她那特有的尖叫音，这样说道。

units.source_en: “Yes, an insolent fellow. We’ll tease him a little to teach him a lesson. There are students from my home province at that school where he teaches.”

units.source_zh: “哼，太狂傲啦，为给他点眼色看，咱们捉弄他一下，他教书的那个学校，有咱们老家的学生呢。”

units.source_en: This was Mr. Kaneda’s voice.
units.source_zh: 这是金田君的声音。

units.source_en: “Who are they?”
units.source_zh: “都是谁？”

units.source_en: Nose asked.
units.source_zh: 鼻子问。

units.source_en: “Tsuneki Pinsuke and Fukuchi Kishago are at that school, so I’ll have them tease him.”

units.source_zh: “津木跳助和福地细螺都在那个学校，让他们去捉弄他好啦。”

units.source_en: I do not know where Mr. Kaneda’s native place is, but I was somewhat surprised that it seemed stocked entirely with people bearing such odd names.
units.source_zh: 我不了解金田君的故乡是哪里，不过这些人的名字都很奇怪，使我吃惊。

units.source_en: Mr. Kaneda went on and asked, “Is that fellow an English teacher?”
units.source_zh: 金田君接下去又问道：“那家伙是教英语的吗？”

units.source_en: “According to the rickshawman’s wife, he teaches something called English readers as his specialty.”
units.source_zh: “听车夫的老婆说，是专教什么英语读本的。”

units.source_en: “Damn him, he’s bound to be a worthless teacher anyway.”
units.source_zh: “他妈的，反正是个糟蛋的教员。”

paragraphs.source_zh: 猫的四条腿虽有如无。不管走到哪里，从来没有发出过笨拙的声响。它宛如凌空飞腾，踏云而行，宛如水中击磬、洞中鼓瑟，宛如饱尝醍醐妙味而冷暖自知一样。我根本不把什么平庸的洋房、模范的厨房、车夫的老婆、听差、烧饭的女仆、小姐、侍女、鼻子夫人、夫人的丈夫放在眼里。我想去哪儿就去哪儿，把想听的都听到之后，伸伸舌头，甩甩尾巴，竖竖胡须，然后悠悠然回来就是了。我尤其对于此道，可谓日本第一名手。甚至连我自己也在怀疑我是否具有经常出现在草双纸故事中那猫精的血统哩。听说蛤蟆的额头上藏有一颗夜明珠，可我的尾巴上却藏有祖传的妙药，这种药不但可以使我蔑视那些神祇、释教、色欲、无常等等观念，甚至也可以把满天下的人都不当回事。我人不知鬼不觉地在金田家廊子里闯来闯去。这比金刚力士踩烂一块魔芋豆腐还要容易得多。想到这里，我不能不佩服起自己的力量来。我想，这完全是托我平时十分珍惜自己尾巴的福，我再也不该将它等闲视之了。于是我决心向我的尾巴大菩萨礼拜一番，来祈祷“猫运长久”。我低下头看了看，好像有点不对头。我必须瞻仰一下自己的尾巴，向它三叩首。我转过身想看看尾巴，可尾巴也自然随着身子转。我扭过头去，想追上它，可它还是保持相同的间隔，跑在前头。看来这尾巴的确是将天地玄黄都收到它那三寸之中的灵物，我是绝对对付不了的。我一直在追自己的尾巴，追了七回半，实在太累，只好作罢。我多少有点天旋地转，简直不知道现在是在哪儿啦。管它呢，我在廊子里到处乱闯。忽然听到拉门里传来鼻子的声音。我想这正是我要找的地方嘛，于是我停下来，把左右两只耳朵斜着掀动了一下，屏息静气地听着。“一个穷教员，竟然这样狂傲！”鼻子发出她那特有的尖叫音，这样说道。“哼，太狂傲啦，为给他点眼色看，咱们捉弄他一下，他教书的那个学校，有咱们老家的学生呢。”这是金田君的声音。“都是谁？”鼻子问。“津木跳助和福地细螺都在那个学校，让他们去捉弄他好啦。”我不了解金田君的故乡是哪里，不过这些人的名字都很奇怪，使我吃惊。金田君接下去又问道：“那家伙是教英语的吗？”“听车夫的老婆说，是专教什么英语读本的。”“他妈的，反正是个糟蛋的教员。”
